narrative: Your law school application was denied because the model estimated an 84% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is a high-risk estimate, not a certainty, but it was strong enough for the admissions decision to go against you. The decision was driven mainly by your academic history, not by your gender or race. Your third-year class standing was the most influential factor and pushed the prediction toward failure; your recorded third-year decile was 1, while accepted students averaged around 5.8. Your first-year standing was the second most influential factor and also pushed toward failure; your first-year decile was 2 versus an accepted average near 6. Your LSAT score was the third most influential factor and pushed in the same direction; a score of 30 is below the accepted-student average of about 37.2. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.20 was close to the accepted average, so it did not offset those concerns. Next, ask admissions for written feedback and whether an appeal or reconsideration is possible. If you reapply, focus on raising your LSAT score, strengthening your academic record, and presenting a concrete bar-exam preparation plan. Also consider applying to additional schools or programs that may weigh your profile differently.
